summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with type 1 diabetes, depression, and alcohol use disorder, was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) after missing insulin due to alcohol use and poor self-care. She presented with vomiting, polyuria, and polydipsia, with a glucose of 751, pH of 7.04, and anion gap of 37. She was treated with an insulin drip and IV fluids, with resolution of DKA and improvement in acute kidney injury, which was attributed to dehydration. Her insulin regimen was adjusted to 15 units of glargine at bedtime with a sliding scale. Psychiatric evaluation led to enrollment in an outpatient alcohol treatment program due to refusal of inpatient admission. Iron deficiency anemia was addressed with continued supplementation. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for primary care, mental health, and diabetes management.
